newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: NITSCHKE SAYS HE'S UNLIKELY TO TAKE ON MORE PATIENTS
Voluntary euthanasia campaigner Phillip Nitschke says he'd be unwise to take on any more patients requesting assisted deaths in the Northern Terrritory.
Dr Nitschke says it's been an exhausting experience obtaining the required approvals for the first two patients to use the Territory Right To Die law, Rod Dent and Janet Mills.
He says he has four more terminally ill patients wanting to access the legislation.
Dr Nitschke says with the forthcoming Senate debate on the Andrews Bill which seeks to overturn assisted deaths, he's unlikely to take on more such patients.
FORD AND AUSTRALIAN MAGNESIUM JOIN FORCES
The Ford company and Australian Magnesium Corporation have joined to produce magnesium to be used in car construction, in a seven-hundred-million dollar magnesium metal project in Queensland.
Ford says the project has benefits for Australian Mining, the Automotive Industry and the Environment.
Magnesium is four times lighter than steel and will make cars lighter and improve fuel efficiency.
Ford has aleady committed 40-million dollars to the pilot stage of the project, that will include a 73-million dollar demonstration plant.
The Australian magnesium smelter will based in Gladstone in central Queensland, and production will be underway by 1999.
Ford will then enter into a multi-million dollar contract with the Gladstone plant to provide magnesium to Ford world-wide.
KENNETT CRITICISES AOC REEF CASINO INVESTMENT
A controversial seven-point-two million dollar investment by the Australian Olympic Committee has come under fire by Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett.
Mr Kennett says the investment in the Cairns Reef Casino is a slap in the eye.
He's questioned whether Victoria should contribute money to the Committee when it next makes a request.
ALICE NIGHTCLUB WINS APPROVAL FOR MEMBERS SCHEME
An Alice Springs nightclub says its had wide approval for a new scheme to screen customers for any criminal record.
Legends nightclub has introduced membership cards, following a number of brawls in its 18-months of operation.
Owner Rohan Miller says applicants are asked if they object to the club looking at their criminal record before granting membership.
He says the Consumer Affairs department and the Liquor Commission are among authorities who approve of the scheme.
WIFE OF MURDERED JOURNO WANTS JUDICIAL INQUIRY
The wife of an Australian journalist, murdered during the 1975 invasion of East Timor, has called for a full judicial inquiry to find out what really happened to those killed.
Shirley Shakleton's comments follow the release of a photograph showing the funeral of five Australian jounalists executed by Indonesian troops.
She says it's unforgivable for the British Government to wait more than 20 years to give the photograph to the victims' families.
Mrs Shackleton says "conspiracy" isn't too big a word to describe what the Australian and Indonesian Governments did.
PORT HEDLAND DISPUTE AFFECTING WA'S FUTURE, SAYS CHAMBER
The Western Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry says unions involved in an industrial stand-off at a project at Port Hedland, are playing with the state's future.

More than six-hundred workers on the one-point-five-billion dollar construction of BHP's hot-briquette iron processing plant, voted yesterday to reject a four per cent pay increase, defying an Industrial Relations Commission recommendation to return to work.
The workers want wages up to 38 per cent above award rates, and a living away from home allowance of 500 dollars-a-week.
The Chamber of Commerce and Industry's Chris Mitsopoulos says the workers haven't been paid since New Year, and the contractors are losing money as well.
Mr Mitsopoulos says the action isn't only affecting the Port Hedland project.
He says there are other parties considering similar projects in the state, who may be swayed by the dispute.
VICTORIA SCORES NEW MAJOR MEET
Victoria has secured another major sports event, with the Australian Athletics Championships linking up with the Nike Track Classic to form a new major meet.
The Championships, to be staged over a two-week carnival, will be held at Melbourne's refurbished Olympic Park from February the 20th.
Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett says the championships will add momentum to Melbourne's bid to host the 2006 Commonwealth Games.
ROCK FESTIVAL CHANGES SHIELD MATCH SCHEDULE
A rock festival has forced a change to next week's Sheffield Shield cricket match in Sydney between South Australia and New South Wales.

A rock concert at the showgrounds adjacent to the Sydney Cricket Ground will be held on Monday January the 27th, the last scheduled day of the match, and is expected to attract over 30-thousand people.
Noise and crowd problems have forced the match to be brought forward by one day, and it will now start on Thursday the 23rd and end on Sunday the 26th.
